environment.app: Vite local server and production preview
environment.firebase: demo-context-health Auth and Firestore emulators only

steps: Sign in with an Auth Emulator Google account and finish onboarding
Open a new workout and enter 오프라인 등
Wait for the 300ms draft debounce and close the browser tab
Open the same origin again and enter a new workout
results.evidence: The workout part text field was restored with value 오프라인 등 after the original tab was closed.

steps: Stop the Firestore Emulator while the workout editor is open
Press 저장하기 and wait nine seconds
Dismiss the error dialog and inspect the editor
results.evidence: At eight seconds the app displayed 서버 저장 확인이 지연되고 있습니다. 작성 내용은 이 기기에 보관했습니다. 네트워크 연결 후 다시 시도해주세요. The editor retained 오프라인 등 and the 저장하기 button was enabled again.

steps: Open the production build on http://127.0.0.1:4173 and wait for service-worker installation
Stop the preview server and close the tab
Open the same origin in a new tab
results.evidence: The complete login screen, logo, and three social login buttons rendered with the origin server stopped.

steps: Open an unvisited origin http://127.0.0.1:4174 while no server is listening
results.evidence: Chrome returned net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. A PWA cannot cold-launch before its app shell has been installed.

steps: Install build A with title Context Health and chunk assets/index-CTMGY3Uk.js
Serve a temporary build B on the same origin with a changed index and JS chunk assets/index-gnS3SYtj.js
Open once to trigger update, close the tab, and reopen
results.evidence: The reopened document title was Context Health B and the changed subtitle ending in B rendered completely. No broken UI or missing-chunk page was observed. Build B existed only under /tmp.

limitations: The browser run directly exercised workout draft restoration; diet draft storage was covered by the shared helper regression and build, not a full browser journey.
The exact offline failure then online retry with the same emulator identity could not be completed because restarting the Auth Emulator deletes its in-memory test account.
No real mobile device, social provider redirect, installed standalone PWA, or production Firebase project was used.
No browser network trace was captured, so absence of old-chunk HTTP 404 is supported by the complete B render rather than request logs.
